Root-cause trace — how a repeatedly-failing document ends up "visibly failed" and why retries don't loop forever:

1. Retries are NOT automatic. There is no Celery auto-retry loop; each retry is explicitly triggered by `DocumentService.retry_document` (api/services/dataset_service.py:2074-2091). Endless retrying is prevented by a Redis guard: for each document it checks `document_{id}_is_retried` (line 2077-2078); if the key already exists it raises `ValueError("Document is being retried, please try again later")` (line 2080) instead of enqueuing another run. Otherwise it flips status to WAITING, sets the flag with a 600s TTL (`redis_client.setex(..., 600, 1)`, line 2086) and dispatches `retry_document_indexing_task.delay(...)` (line 2091). So concurrent/repeat retries are blocked until the current attempt finishes or the TTL expires.

2. The async worker `retry_document_indexing_task` (api/tasks/retry_document_indexing_task.py:23-126) does the work per document. On any failure it RECORDS the failure and STOPS: the except block at lines 111-118 sets `document.indexing_status = IndexingStatus.ERROR`, `document.error = str(ex)`, `document.stopped_at = naive_utc_now()`, commits (lines 112-116), then deletes the `..._is_retried` Redis flag (line 118) — releasing the guard but leaving the document in the terminal ERROR state (it does not re-enqueue). The subscription/vector-limit precheck failure path does the same (lines 66-72).

3. Inside the actual indexing, failures funnel through `IndexingRunner.run` (api/core/indexing_runner.py:68-126). Its except handlers (lines 121-126) call `_handle_indexing_error` (indexing_runner.py:57-66), which is where the failure is durably recorded: it loads the document, sets `indexing_status = IndexingStatus.ERROR`, `error = <message>`, `stopped_at`, and commits (lines 62-66). (Note: `DocumentIsPausedError` is deliberately re-raised at line 119-120 and NOT turned into ERROR, so a pause isn't misreported as failure.)

Net: the "retry stops" because retrying is manual and gated by the `document_{id}_is_retried` Redis flag (dataset_service.py:2078-2086), and the "visibly failed" state is the `IndexingStatus.ERROR` + `error`/`stopped_at` fields written by `_handle_indexing_error` (indexing_runner.py:62-66) and the retry task's except block (retry_document_indexing_task.py:112-116). That ERROR status is the terminal, user-visible failure record.</answer>

Force-stop-on-overrun lives in the app queue manager's listen loop, driven by a wall-clock deadline.

Root cause / trace:
- The generation is consumed via `AppQueueManager.listen()` at `api/core/app/apps/base_app_queue_manager.py:55`. Before looping it sets `listen_timeout = dify_config.APP_MAX_EXECUTION_TIME` (`base_app_queue_manager.py:61`) and records `start_time` (`:62`).
- On every `finally` of each 1s queue poll it computes `elapsed_time = time.time() - start_time` (`:75`). When `elapsed_time >= listen_timeout` (i.e. the run has gone on too long) — the same branch also covers manual stop via `self._is_stopped()` — it force-publishes a stop event: `self.publish(QueueStopEvent(stopped_by=QueueStopEvent.StopBy.USER_MANUAL), PublishFrom.TASK_PIPELINE)` at `base_app_queue_manager.py:76-81`. So the emitted internal event is a `QueueStopEvent` (`event = QueueEvent.STOP`) with `stopped_by = StopBy.USER_MANUAL`.
- `APP_MAX_EXECUTION_TIME` is the configured cap (default 1200s) at `api/configs/feature/__init__.py:83-86`.
- `QueueStopEvent` / its `StopBy` enum and `get_stop_reason()` are defined at `api/core/app/entities/queue_entities.py:486-515` (USER_MANUAL → "Stopped by user.").

What the client sees (the emitted downstream/stream event) depends on app type:
- Easy-UI (chat/completion/agent) pipeline: `QueueStopEvent` is matched at `api/core/app/task_pipeline/easy_ui_based_generate_task_pipeline.py:276`, handled by `_handle_stop(event)` (`:281`, def at `:433`), then the run is closed by yielding a `MessageEndStreamResponse` via `_message_end_to_stream_response()` (`:296-297`, `:463`).
- Workflow app pipeline: `QueueStopEvent` matched at `api/core/app/apps/workflow/generate_task_pipeline.py:729`, handled by `_handle_workflow_failed_and_stop_events` (`:527`), which sets `status = WorkflowExecutionStatus.STOPPED`, `error = event.get_stop_reason()` (`:544-545`) and emits a `WorkflowFinishStreamResponse` with STOPPED status via `workflow_finish_to_stream_response` (`:547-555`).
- Advanced-chat pipeline handles it analogously at `api/core/app/apps/advanced_chat/generate_task_pipeline.py:753`, also mapping to `WorkflowExecutionStatus.STOPPED` (`:769`).

Summary: an over-long generation is cut off by the `APP_MAX_EXECUTION_TIME` deadline check in `AppQueueManager.listen()` (`base_app_queue_manager.py:75-81`), which emits a `QueueStopEvent(stopped_by=USER_MANUAL)`; the task pipelines then surface this as a message-end (easy UI) or a STOPPED `WorkflowFinishStreamResponse` (workflow/advanced-chat) with reason "Stopped by user."

Root cause / trace: the "run forever" guard is the workflow's max-execution-time (and max-steps) limit, enforced by an execution-limits graph layer whose abort is turned into a workflow-failed event.

1. Config knob: `WORKFLOW_MAX_EXECUTION_TIME` (default 1200s) and `WORKFLOW_MAX_EXECUTION_STEPS` (default 500) are defined in `api/configs/feature/__init__.py:784-787` and `:779-782`.

2. Wiring: `WorkflowEntry._init_graph_engine`/setup registers the limit layer in `api/core/workflow/workflow_entry.py:228-229`:
   `ExecutionLimitsLayer(max_steps=dify_config.WORKFLOW_MAX_EXECUTION_STEPS, max_time=dify_config.WORKFLOW_MAX_EXECUTION_TIME)` then `self.graph_engine.layer(limits_layer)`. (Confirmed by the layer/wiring test at `api/tests/unit_tests/core/workflow/test_workflow_entry_helpers.py:282,322`.) `ExecutionLimitsLayer` itself lives in the external `graphon` package (`from graphon.graph_engine.layers import ... ExecutionLimitsLayer`, workflow_entry.py:37), not in the Dify repo.

3. Force-stop mechanism: when the run exceeds `max_time`/`max_steps`, the layer force-stops the engine the same way Dify's in-repo layers do — by sending an `AbortCommand(command_type=CommandType.ABORT, reason=...)` over the engine's command channel. This is the exact pattern of the in-repo analog `LLMQuotaLayer._send_abort_command` / `_abort_before_node_run` at `api/core/app/workflow/layers/llm_quota.py:144-157` (and `:123-137`). The aborted engine emits a `GraphRunAbortedEvent` (carrying the abort `reason`).

4. Event translation (this is the event Dify emits for the cut-off): `WorkflowBasedAppRunner._handle_event` maps the engine event to a queue event in `api/core/app/apps/workflow_app_runner.py:426-427`:
   `case GraphRunAbortedEvent(): self._publish_event(QueueWorkflowFailedEvent(error=event.reason or "Unknown error", exceptions_count=0))`.
   (If the engine surfaces it as a plain failure instead, the adjacent `case GraphRunFailedEvent()` at `:422-425` also produces a `QueueWorkflowFailedEvent`; `WorkflowEntry.run` additionally yields `GraphRunFailedEvent(error=str(e))` on any escaped exception at `workflow_entry.py:249`.) The persistence layer records the abort via `WorkflowPersistenceLayer._handle_graph_run_aborted` (`api/core/app/workflow/layers/persistence.py:125,197`).

5. Client-facing terminal event: the `QueueWorkflowFailedEvent` is consumed by `WorkflowAppGenerateTaskPipeline._handle_workflow_failed_and_stop_events` (`api/core/app/apps/workflow/generate_task_pipeline.py:527-555`), which sets `status = WorkflowExecutionStatus.FAILED` and yields a `workflow_finished` stream response (failed), i.e. the run is terminated with a failed workflow-finish event rather than running forever. (Advanced-chat has the analogous `_handle_stop_event` at `api/core/app/apps/advanced_chat/generate_task_pipeline.py:751`.)

Summary chain: WORKFLOW_MAX_EXECUTION_TIME → ExecutionLimitsLayer (workflow_entry.py:228-229) → AbortCommand over command channel → GraphRunAbortedEvent → QueueWorkflowFailedEvent (workflow_app_runner.py:426-427) → workflow_finished/FAILED stream response (generate_task_pipeline.py:527-555).

Note: the agent-loop analog exists but does NOT emit an event — `cot_agent_runner`/`fc_agent_runner` cap iterations and instead raise `AgentMaxIterationError` (api/core/agent/fc_agent_runner.py:230, cot_agent_runner.py:182), so it is not the "emits an event" path the ticket asks about.

Failure recording and the "no endless retry" behavior are split across three files. There is no automatic infinite retry loop in Dify — each retry is a single, user-triggered Celery task run, and a repeated failure lands the document in a terminal ERROR state.

1) Where an indexing failure is recorded (the primary sink)
`IndexingRunner._handle_indexing_error` — api/core/indexing_runner.py:57-66. On any exception during indexing it sets the document to the terminal failed state and commits:
- `document.indexing_status = IndexingStatus.ERROR` (line 62)
- `document.error = str(error_message)` (line 63; uses `error.description` if present)
- `document.stopped_at = naive_utc_now()` (line 64), then `db.session.commit()` (line 66)
This is invoked from the generic `except Exception` / `except ProviderTokenNotInitError` handlers in `run()` (api/core/indexing_runner.py:121-126), and likewise from `run_in_splitting_status` and `run_in_indexing_status`. `IndexingStatus.ERROR` is defined in api/models/enums.py (IndexingStatus, ~line 129-139). This ERROR status + error message is what makes the document "visibly failed" in the UI.

2) The retry task itself, and its own failure sink
`retry_document_indexing_task` — api/tasks/retry_document_indexing_task.py:23-126 (a `@shared_task(queue="dataset")`, so it runs exactly once per dispatch — it does not re-enqueue itself). It resets the doc to PARSING and calls `IndexingRunner().run([document])` (lines 98-109). If that raises, the task's own `except Exception` block again records the failure terminally: `indexing_status = ERROR`, `error = str(ex)`, `stopped_at = naive_utc_now()`, commit (lines 111-119). A pre-check for the billing/vector-space limit does the same ERROR write and returns early (lines 61-72). In every failure path it also calls `redis_client.delete(retry_indexing_cache_key)` (lines 71, 110, 118).

3) Where the retry "stops" / cannot be repeated endlessly
`DocumentService.retry_document` — api/services/dataset_service.py:2074-2091. Before dispatching the task it enforces a Redis guard keyed `document_{id}_is_retried`:
- If the key already exists it raises `ValueError("Document is being retried, please try again later")` (lines 2078-2080), blocking a concurrent/duplicate retry.
- Otherwise it sets the doc to WAITING and sets the flag with a 600s TTL: `redis_client.setex(retry_indexing_cache_key, 600, 1)` (line 2086), then dispatches `retry_document_indexing_task.delay(...)` (line 2091).

Net trace: indexing fails → `_handle_indexing_error` writes status=ERROR/error/stopped_at (indexing_runner.py:57-66) → document is visibly failed. A retry is only ever a manual, one-shot re-dispatch gated by the `document_{id}_is_retried` Redis flag; the flag is cleared and the doc re-marked ERROR on repeated failure (retry_document_indexing_task.py:111-118), so the document simply stays in the terminal ERROR state rather than being retried automatically.

Root cause / trace — this is Dify's agent-loop iteration cap (a runaway agent that keeps calling tools instead of finishing), which force-stops the "generation" and surfaces it as a QueueErrorEvent.

1. Config / limit. The per-agent cap is `max_iteration` (default 10) on `AgentEntity` — api/core/agent/entities.py:86. Each runner clamps it: `max_iteration_steps = min(app_config.agent.max_iteration, 99) + 1` (fc_agent_runner.py:56, cot_agent_runner.py:80).

2. The bounded loop. Both runners iterate `while function_call_state and iteration_step <= max_iteration_steps` — api/core/agent/fc_agent_runner.py:81 and api/core/agent/cot_agent_runner.py:106. On the final permitted step the tool list is stripped (`prompt_messages_tools = []` / `self._prompt_messages_tools = []`) to coax a final answer — fc_agent_runner.py:84-86, cot_agent_runner.py:110-112.

3. The hard cut-off. If, on that last iteration, the model STILL insists on calling a tool, the run is aborted:
   - Function-calling runner: `if iteration_step == max_iteration_steps and tool_calls: raise AgentMaxIterationError(...)` — api/core/agent/fc_agent_runner.py:229-230.
   - Chain-of-thought runner: `if iteration_step == max_iteration_steps and scratchpad.action and action_name != "final answer": raise AgentMaxIterationError(...)` — api/core/agent/cot_agent_runner.py:180-182.
   The exception itself is defined in api/core/agent/errors.py:1-8 (`AgentMaxIterationError`, a plain `Exception`).

4. What event it emits. The runner's `run()` generator is driven inside the agent-chat worker in api/core/app/apps/agent_chat/app_generator.py:257. `AgentMaxIterationError` is a bare `Exception` (not `ValueError`), so it falls through to the catch-all `except Exception as e:` at app_generator.py:277-279, which calls `queue_manager.publish_error(e, PublishFrom.APPLICATION_MANAGER)`. `publish_error` (api/core/app/apps/base_app_queue_manager.py:108-115) wraps it as `QueueErrorEvent(error=e)` (base_app_queue_manager.py:115).

So: the run is force-stopped by the `max_iteration` guard in the agent runners (fc_agent_runner.py:229 / cot_agent_runner.py:180), raising `AgentMaxIterationError`, and the event ultimately emitted onto the generation queue is a **QueueErrorEvent** carrying that error.

(For reference, workflow/graph runs have a separate limiter — `ExecutionLimitsLayer(max_steps=WORKFLOW_MAX_EXECUTION_STEPS, max_time=WORKFLOW_MAX_EXECUTION_TIME)` attached in api/core/workflow/workflow_entry.py:228-230 — but that layer lives in the external `graphon` package, not in this repo, and governs workflows rather than agent "generations.")

Where the failure is recorded and the retry stops (Dify, api/):

1. Retry is manual/user-triggered, not an automatic infinite loop. DatasetService.retry_document (api/services/dataset_service.py:2074-2091) is the entry point. Before dispatching it sets a Redis guard key `document_{id}_is_retried` via setex with a 600s TTL (line 2077, 2086), and if that key already exists it raises "Document is being retried, please try again later" (lines 2078-2080). This is the mechanism that stops a document from being retried endlessly/concurrently — only one retry per document can be in flight, and further retry requests are rejected until it clears. It flips the doc to IndexingStatus.WAITING (line 2082) and fires retry_document_indexing_task.delay (line 2091).

2. The async worker retry_document_indexing_task (api/tasks/retry_document_indexing_task.py:23) cleans old segments/vectors, sets PARSING, and runs IndexingRunner().run([document]) (lines 98-109). It always deletes the Redis retry guard on completion (line 110 on success; lines 118 on failure) so the doc is not locked forever.

3. Where a repeated failure becomes visibly failed: if indexing raises, the task's except block (retry_document_indexing_task.py:111-119) sets `document.indexing_status = IndexingStatus.ERROR`, records `document.error = str(ex)` and `stopped_at = naive_utc_now()`, commits (lines 112-116), and deletes the retry cache key (line 118). The quota pre-check has the same terminal-ERROR path (lines 61-72).

4. The underlying IndexingRunner also records the failure independently: IndexingRunner.run wraps the whole pipeline and routes every exception to _handle_indexing_error (api/core/indexing_runner.py:125-126), which sets indexing_status = IndexingStatus.ERROR, error, and stopped_at and commits (indexing_runner.py:57-66). (DocumentIsPausedError is re-raised, not marked error; ObjectDeletedError is skipped.)

Net trace: a document that keeps failing does NOT auto-retry — each retry is an explicit user action guarded by the `_is_retried` Redis key. When a retry attempt fails, the failure is persisted as IndexingStatus.ERROR with the error message and stopped_at on the Document row (the visibly-failed terminal state), and the Redis guard is cleared so the row simply sits in ERROR until a human triggers another retry. There is no server-side loop that keeps re-attempting on its own. Key recording sites: retry_document_indexing_task.py:112-116 and indexing_runner.py:57-66 (via :125-126); retry-stop/guard: dataset_service.py:2077-2086.</answer>

Dify force-stops a runaway generation on a wall-clock timeout in the app queue manager's listener, not on an iteration/step count.

Mechanism — `AppQueueManager.listen()` at `api/core/app/apps/base_app_queue_manager.py:55-87`:
- Line 61: the listen timeout is set to `dify_config.APP_MAX_EXECUTION_TIME` (the ceiling on how long a single generation/task may run).
- Line 62: records `start_time = time.time()` when listening begins.
- Lines 65-73: the loop pulls messages off the internal `queue.Queue` (`self._q.get(timeout=1)`) and yields them to the client.
- Lines 74-81 (the per-iteration `finally`): it computes `elapsed_time = time.time() - start_time` (line 75), and when `elapsed_time >= listen_timeout` (or the task was manually stopped via `self._is_stopped()`) it force-terminates the run by publishing a stop event: `self.publish(QueueStopEvent(stopped_by=QueueStopEvent.StopBy.USER_MANUAL), PublishFrom.TASK_PIPELINE)` (lines 79-81). (Lines 83-85 additionally emit periodic `QueuePingEvent`s to keep the SSE connection alive.)

Event emitted — `QueueStopEvent` (`event = QueueEvent.STOP`), defined at `api/core/app/entities/queue_entities.py:486-515`, with `stopped_by = QueueStopEvent.StopBy.USER_MANUAL` (the `StopBy` enum is at lines 491-499; note the timeout path reuses the USER_MANUAL reason rather than a dedicated timeout reason).

Downstream, that `QueueStopEvent` is consumed by the generate-task pipeline and converted into a terminal stop response — e.g. `WorkflowAppGenerateTaskPipeline._handle_workflow_failed_and_stop_events()` at `api/core/app/apps/workflow/generate_task_pipeline.py:527-555`, which handles `QueueStopEvent` and finalizes the run/stream (emitting the workflow-finished/stop stream response to the client).

So: the cut-off point is the time-budget check inside `AppQueueManager.listen()` (base_app_queue_manager.py:75-81), triggered by `APP_MAX_EXECUTION_TIME`, and the event it emits is a `QueueStopEvent` (QueueEvent.STOP, StopBy.USER_MANUAL).

Root-cause trace — indexing does NOT auto-retry endlessly; failure is recorded terminally as IndexingStatus.ERROR and the task simply returns.

1) Where a failed index is recorded (the terminal "visibly failed" state):
- `api/core/indexing_runner.py:68` `IndexingRunner.run()` wraps each document's extract/transform/load in try/except. Any non-pause exception falls to `except Exception as e:` (indexing_runner.py:125-126) which calls `_handle_indexing_error(document_id, e)`.
- `_handle_indexing_error` (indexing_runner.py:57-66) sets `document.indexing_status = IndexingStatus.ERROR`, `document.error = <message>`, `document.stopped_at = naive_utc_now()` and commits. 2) Why the retry stops (no endless retry):

Pre-flight limit failures also write ERROR directly and `return` (document_indexing_task.py:81-92). => a failed document ends at ERROR and stops.

3) Retry is user-initiated and one-shot (bounded), not a loop:
- `DatasetService.retry_document` (`api/services/dataset_service.py:2073-2091`): guards with redis key `document_{id}_is_retried`; if present raises "Document is being retried" (:2078-2080), else sets status WAITING, sets the key with a 600s TTL (`redis_client.setex(..., 600, 1)` at :2086) and enqueues `retry_document_indexing_task.delay(...)` (:2091). The 600s flag prevents re-triggering while one retry is in flight. (Entry point `DatasetService.retry_document_indexing` at dataset_service.py:2077-2091 area / task dispatch at :2091.)

On failure its own `except Exception as ex` (:111-119) again writes `indexing_status=ERROR`, `error`, `stopped_at`, commits, and deletes the retry cache key (:118). It does not re-enqueue itself. => each retry click = exactly one attempt, then back to a visible ERROR state.

Summary: There is no automatic retry backoff loop for document indexing. A repeatedly-failing document lands in IndexingStatus.ERROR via `IndexingRunner._handle_indexing_error` (indexing_runner.py:57-66); the Celery tasks catch-and-return without requeue (document_indexing_task.py:119-121); and manual retries are gated one-at-a-time by the `document_{id}_is_retried` redis flag and each terminate in ERROR again (retry_document_indexing_task.py:111-119, dataset_service.py:2077-2091).</answer>

The billing/vector-space guard earlier (lines ~66-77) also writes ERROR + error + stopped_at and returns.

- Guard against re-triggering while a retry is already in flight: `DocumentService.retry_document` (api/services/dataset_service.py:2074-2091) checks a Redis key `document_{id}_is_retried`; if present it raises `"Document is being retried, please try again later"` (lines 2077-2080), otherwise it flips status to WAITING, dispatches the task, and sets the key with a 600s TTL (`redis_client.setex(..., 600, 1)`, line 2086). The task deletes that key on every terminal outcome (success or ERROR), so the lock plus the terminal ERROR state are what bound retries.
- Controller-level guard: api/controllers/console/datasets/datasets_document.py:1298-1300 rejects retrying a document whose `indexing_status == IndexingStatus.COMPLETED` (`DocumentAlreadyFinishedError`); only non-completed (e.g. ERROR/PAUSED) docs are added to `retry_documents` and passed to `retry_document` at line 1306.

NET BEHAVIOR: a repeatedly-failing document always lands back in `IndexingStatus.ERROR` with `error` and `stopped_at` populated (indexing_runner.py:62-65 or retry_document_indexing_task.py exception block), and it stays there until a user explicitly retries; the 600s Redis lock prevents rapid re-fire, so it is not retried endlessly on its own.

2) There is no self-triggered re-run. `indexing_runner.run` iterates the given documents once and, on Exception, just records ERROR and moves on (no requeue). So a repeatedly-failing doc simply stays in ERROR — the loop naturally stops.

3) Retry only happens when a user explicitly calls the retry endpoint. The controller (api/controllers/console/datasets/datasets_document.py:1283-1306) collects the requested docs, rejects already-COMPLETED ones (`DocumentAlreadyFinishedError`, lines 1299-1300), and calls `DocumentService.retry_document`.

Because the key is cleared, a subsequent manual retry is allowed, but nothing re-issues it automatically; the document remains in ERROR until a human retries.

Trace:

1. Limit is configured. `WORKFLOW_MAX_EXECUTION_TIME` (default 1200 seconds) and `WORKFLOW_MAX_EXECUTION_STEPS` (default 500) are defined in `api/configs/feature/__init__.py:784` and `:779`.

2. The cutoff is installed as a graph-engine layer. In `WorkflowEntry.__init__`, `api/core/workflow/workflow_entry.py:227-231` builds `ExecutionLimitsLayer(max_steps=dify_config.WORKFLOW_MAX_EXECUTION_STEPS, max_time=dify_config.WORKFLOW_MAX_EXECUTION_TIME)` and attaches it via `self.graph_engine.layer(limits_layer)`. (`ExecutionLimitsLayer` is imported at `workflow_entry.py:37` from the external `graphon.graph_engine.layers`; it is what watches elapsed time/steps and aborts the run once the wall-clock exceeds `max_time`.)

3. On abort the engine emits `GraphRunAbortedEvent` (from `graphon.graph_events`). Dify consumes it in `WorkflowBasedAppRunner._handle_event`, `api/core/app/apps/workflow_app_runner.py:426-427`, where the `case GraphRunAbortedEvent():` branch publishes a `QueueWorkflowFailedEvent(error=event.reason or "Unknown error", exceptions_count=0)` onto the app queue (event class imported at `workflow_app_runner.py:61`).

4. Persistence marks the run STOPPED. `WorkflowPersistenceLayer._handle_graph_run_aborted`, `api/core/app/workflow/layers/persistence.py:197-206` (dispatched from the `case GraphRunAbortedEvent()` at `:125`), sets `execution.status = WorkflowExecutionStatus.STOPPED`, records `error_message = event.reason or "Workflow execution aborted"`, and fails any still-running node executions.

So: force-stop is driven by graphon's `ExecutionLimitsLayer` (max_time = WORKFLOW_MAX_EXECUTION_TIME) wired in at `api/core/workflow/workflow_entry.py:228`; the engine-level event emitted is `GraphRunAbortedEvent`, which Dify translates into a `QueueWorkflowFailedEvent` at `api/core/app/apps/workflow_app_runner.py:426-427` and records as a STOPPED WorkflowExecution.

Note: this is the workflow/advanced-chat generation path. The separate user-initiated stop (AppTaskService.stop_task, QueueStopEvent) is a different mechanism; the automatic "ran too long" cutoff is the ExecutionLimitsLayer/GraphRunAbortedEvent path above.
